hooks.text: An orange dwarf star is hurtling straight toward our solar system.
In 1.29 million years, a distant star will pass through our comet reservoir.
A passing star will soon become the brightest object in our night sky.

title: The Star on a Collision Course With Our Solar System
description: An orange dwarf star named Gliese 710 is heading straight for the outer edges of our solar system, threatening to trigger a relentless shower of comets.

beats.text: An orange dwarf star is hurtling straight toward our solar system.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of an orange dwarf star in deep space, 2020

beats.text: Sitting 62.3 light-years away in Serpens, precision data from the Gaia spacecraft reveals a shocking path.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of the Gaia spacecraft mapping stars in space, 2013

beats.text: Astronomers tracked Gliese 710 heading toward us at roughly 14.5 kilometers per second.
beats.visual: Stellar classification chart highlighting K-type stars, 2018

beats.text: In about 1.29 million years, it will plow directly into our solar system's Oort cloud.
beats.visual: NASA diagram of the Oort cloud surrounding the solar system, 2010

beats.text: At a closest approach of 10,520 astronomical units, it becomes the brightest object in our night sky besides the Sun, Moon, and Venus.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a bright star in the night sky, 2021
queries: bright star in night sky artist concept

beats.text: While major planets remain safe, its immense gravity will dislodge millions of icy comets.
beats.visual: Illustration of a comet passing the inner solar system, 2015
queries: comet passing inner solar system art

beats.text: This gravitational disturbance triggers ten naked-eye comets per year, proving an orange dwarf star is hurtling straight toward our solar system.
emphasis: orange dwarf star is hurtling straight toward our solar system
beats.visual: NASA illustration of a comet approaching the Sun, 2017
